9.11.4. qnav.util.rng

9.11.4.1. rng.py

summary:

Provides alternative means for pseudo-random number generation. This module contains implementations for controlled random number generation, subject to realistic factors. Currently, this only supplies gaussian-markov random walk based number generation.

authors:
Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk
version:

1.0.0 - First implementation of module.

class qnav.util.rng.GaussianMarkov(corr_time: float, psd: float, output_shape: int | tuple[int] = 1, start_time: float = 0, seed: int = None)[source]

Gaussian Markov First-Order Random Walk Model. Generates controlled random numbers following a Gaussian Markov random walk. Can be used to replace typical normal random number generation.

get_random(clock_time: float) → float | ndarray[source]

Generates random number(s) for requested time and shape. Calling this method continues the random walk to the given time in seconds. Calling with a time earlier than that of the last measurement will result in a value error due to illegal state.

Parameters:

clock_time (float) – The current simulation clock time.

Returns:

Randomly generated number(s).

Return type:

float | np.ndarray

reset(clock_time: float = 0) → None[source]

Resets the internal state of the random walk, clearing previous history and information.

Parameters:

clock_time (float) – Optional new initialisation clock time. By default this is 0 seconds.

property output_shape: int | tuple[int]

Returns the output shape numbers are being generated for. This is the dimensions of the output of the number generator.

Returns:

Output shape for random number generation.

Return type:

int | tuple[int]

property last_value: float | ndarray | None

Returns the last random value generated.

Returns:

Last value returned by generator.

Return type:

float | np.ndarray | None

property last_time: float

Returns time of last number(s) generated in seconds.

Returns:

Time of last number(s) generated.

Return type:

float
